note.explanation: Allotropy means that the same element can exist in different structural forms, and those forms can have different physical and chemical properties. Carbon has forms such as diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene; sulphur has rhombic and monoclinic forms.
examples: Carbon: diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀).
Sulphur: rhombic and monoclinic sulphur; rhombic sulphur is more stable.
note.checkAnswer: Carbon and sulphur are elements that show allotropy.
note.simple: One element can have different forms because its atoms can be arranged differently. These forms may have different properties.

written.text: Q1.2. What are allotropic forms? Explain the allotropic forms of carbon and sulphur. How does coal differ from diamond?
written.finalAnswer: Allotropic forms are different structural forms of the same element that can have quite different physical and chemical properties. Carbon's forms include diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀). Diamond has a giant macromolecular structure; graphite has layers of hexagonal carbon rings; fullerene C₆₀ has a cage-like sphere made from pentagons and hexagons. Sulphur has rhombic and monoclinic crystalline forms, and rhombic sulphur is more stable. Coal is an amorphous, impure form of carbon, whereas diamond is a crystalline form of carbon.

explain.title: What allotropy means
explain.body: Elements may exist in more than one structural forms which can exhibit quite different physical and chemical properties. These forms are called allotropic forms and phenomenon is called allotropy. In simple terms, the same element can have different arrangements and properties.

explain.title: Carbon has different structures
explain.body: Carbon has three main allotropic forms: diamond, graphite and Buckminster fullerene. Diamond has a giant macromolecular structure. Graphite has layers of hexagonal carbon rings. Buckminster fullerene (C₆₀) is a cage-like sphere made of carbon atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons.

explain.title: Sulphur has two crystalline forms
explain.body: Sulphur exists as rhombic and monoclinic crystals. Remember the comparison: rhombic sulphur is more stable than monoclinic sulphur.

explain.title: Remember the fullerene facts
explain.body: The fullerene structure is not charged, has no boundaries and has no unpaired electrons. Fullerene C₆₀ has a low melting point, is soft and cannot conduct electricity.

mistakes: Do not confuse allotropes with compounds: O₂ and O₃ are forms of the element oxygen, while compounds contain different elements.
Do not mix up the structures: diamond is giant and macromolecular; graphite is layered; fullerene is cage-like.
Do not say monoclinic sulphur is more stable; rhombic sulphur is more stable.
When comparing graphene and graphite, make clear that graphene is one layer and graphite consists of many layers.
Do not omit the stability comparison when asked to explain sulphur's allotropic forms.
